selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: Why is the universe compared to a book or page?
questions.answer: Because creation is presented as something full of meaning that can be read and understood.

questions.question: What does the image of a golden pen suggest about creation?
questions.answer: It suggests beauty, value, skill, and deliberate making.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the “pages” of the world’s book?
questions.answer: It describes them as countless dimensions and layers beyond easy measure.

questions.question: Why does the passage stress that the world’s pages are limitless?
questions.answer: It stresses that Allah’s signs and meanings cannot be reduced to a small number.

questions.question: What does calling every being an embodied word teach about creation?
questions.answer: It teaches that created things are not meaningless objects but carry meaning and purpose.

questions.question: What is the benefit of describing each being as meaningful?
questions.answer: It helps the reader see purpose and wisdom in creation.

questions.question: What does the unity of many voices saying the same truth suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests harmony in creation and shared witness to one Creator.

questions.question: What does the line about every thing containing a sign teach about neglecting reflection?
questions.answer: It suggests that failing to reflect means overlooking clear reminders.

questions.question: What is one main idea of the whole passage?
questions.answer: The whole universe, in all its parts, points clearly and together to Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What overall conclusion does the target passage lead to?
questions.answer: It leads to the conclusion that the whole universe is a unified testimony to Allah’s oneness, truth, and life.

questions.question: How does the image of a colored page help the reader think about the world?
questions.answer: It helps the reader see the world as rich, beautiful, and full of signs.

questions.question: What does this image suggest about the relationship between creation and knowledge of Allah?
questions.answer: It suggests that creation helps people know Allah through His signs.

questions.question: Why are the dimensions of the world’s book described as endless?
questions.answer: To show the vastness and depth of creation’s meanings.

questions.question: What part does time play in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: Time carries countless events that also point to Allah.

questions.question: What phrase in the passage expresses the testimony of all things to tawhid?
questions.answer: The passage says that all things together witness that only Allah is worthy of worship.

questions.question: What truth is announced by all things together?
questions.answer: They announce Allah’s absolute oneness.

questions.question: What does the mention of the Living One add to the meaning of the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that the One pointed to by creation is fully living and gives life.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that every thing contains a sign?
questions.answer: It can be inferred that evidence of Allah is widespread and constant.

questions.question: Which is the better summary of the passage: creation is silent and empty, or creation is full of meaningful signs of Allah?
questions.answer: Creation is full of meaningful signs of Allah.

questions.question: What comparison structures the opening of the passage?
questions.answer: The world is compared to a written text that can be read.

questions.question: In that metaphor, what do the visible forms in creation function as?
questions.answer: They function as written signs that carry meaning.

questions.question: How does the passage move from one page to many pages or layers?
questions.answer: It expands from one image of a page to the idea that the world has endless levels of meaning.

questions.question: How does it describe the events that occur through time?
questions.answer: It describes them as many works unfolding without number.

questions.question: What can students infer from calling a being a “word”?
questions.answer: They can infer that it points beyond itself to its Maker.
